schemas.gloss_en: דאמר קרא 'בכור בניך תתן לי', 'כן תעשה לצאנך'; 'מלאתך ודמעך לא תאחר', 'כן תעשה לשורך' (26b.10-11) -- the firstborn-son clause is paired with the flock and the first-fruits clause with the ox. Per Steinsaltz (not stated in the Hebrew): as the son is redeemed at thirty days so the flock at thirty; as first-fruits come at Shavuot, fifty days on, so the ox at fifty

grounds.gloss_en: איפוך אנא! -- reverse the pairing (the ox at thirty, the flock at fifty). The exchange that follows rides here (header: gate gap): the stam answers מסתברא דמקדם למקדם, דמאחר לדמאחר (the earlier clause to the earlier animal, the later to the later), and counters itself אדרבה, דסמיך ליה לדסמיך ליה! (on the contrary, the adjacent clause to the adjacent animal) -- left unanswered; the sugya turns to אלא אמר רבא

objections.gloss_en: ואימא: שיתין! -- [if the ox gets another 'doing'] say sixty [days]!

answered_by.gloss_en: לא מסרך הכתוב אלא לחכמים -- Scripture handed [the measure] only to the sages
